startup.name: Talking Computers
startup.one_liner: Real-time interaction models for voice agents
startup.description: Talking Computers is an AI lab building real time interaction models so voice agents are both capable and human like, measured by time to first audio token. Customers would be voice agent builders and enterprises paying for model API usage. Team of 2 in San Francisco, Winter 2026 batch. Its claim of sitting at the Pareto frontier of intelligence and interactivity is unverified.

yc_acceptance.basis: Already in the Winter 2026 batch, so reported for completeness. Start at the roughly 1 percent prior, lift for a research style technical team in a category investors fund heavily, and discount because there is no stated traction and model labs need capital that a two person team may not convince investors it can use well.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because foundation voice models are capital hungry and led by well funded players (Vapi W21 on top of others, PlayAI W23 acquired by Meta), and a two person lab without public customers must show a model result that beats open models from larger teams.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B --tag AI: seed 45% / 52% / 58%, cond 52% (n=533). Timing: time_to_milestones.csv era:2022+ months_to_seed p25 3, p50 6, p75 14.2.
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor of 0.52 is the ever reached figure. The window is 10 months from 2026-01-05 to 2026-11-17; era 2022+ seed timing has a median of 6 months and p75 of 14, so roughly 60 percent of eventual raisers are inside it, about 0.31. I add a small lift for a hot AI model category where voice labs drew large early rounds, giving 0.34, well under 1.25 times the windowed figure. The odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round of $1M to $3M, typical when a two to four person team raises from angels and micro funds soon after demo day. Voice model teams drew larger early checks in 2025 than typical software, so I keep the upper bands slightly fatter within the default shape.

Institutional seed of $3M to $6M, near the 2022 and later median of $3.5M in round_benchmarks.csv, which includes the YC deal so it reads low. Voice model teams drew larger early checks in 2025 than typical software, so I keep the upper bands slightly fatter within the default shape.
Larger institutional seed of $6M to $12M, where press covered 2026 raises had their median of $6.0M; needs live revenue or a standout founder story.
Upside seed above $12M, seen in 2025 voice, document and agent categories when a lab style team is bid up by several funds.

ladder.why_it_fails: Investors may pass because a model lab needs compute money and a clear edge, and a two person team with no named customers has to show an actual benchmark lead over open voice models. PlayAI (W23) did raise a $21M seed and sold to Meta, but it had product and developer users first. The miss would be an acquihire or a small round that does not clear the $1M line.

bands.rationale: Thin or small Series A, common for vertical software with early but modest revenue.
Central band around the 2022 and later Series A median of $15M with p25 $11M.
Strong growth round led by a top tier fund.
Upside where the category is hot and revenue compounds fast.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A needs revenue from voice agent builders or enterprises and a model that stays ahead as open and big lab voice models improve. Within the months left after a seed the team would need compute scale, a product surface and customers. Vapi went from seed to Series A in about thirteen months, which is the best case; most voice companies in the records have not shown an A.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B --tag AI: series_b cond 20% (n=70), ever 3% known-only.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Series B inside a window of 10 months is rare: months_to_series_b has a median of 36 to 47 months from the batch start in time_to_milestones.csv, so almost no company reaches it this fast. Only a breakout would.

bands.rationale: Thin Series B or extension round, used when growth slowed after the Series A and investors price the company on revenue multiples alone.
Central band; 2022 and later Series B median is $40M.
Hot company band; 2022 and later post money median is $600M.
Breakout upside where one lead investor competes hard for a category leader with fast revenue growth and strong net retention.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series B inside 10 months of the start would need a leap like Vapi, which took more than two years to its Series B. For a two person lab this is only a breakout case, where a frontier voice model gets large enterprise adoption and is bid up by several funds.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B --tag AI: series_c cond 14% (n=14), ever 0% known-only.
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor is conditional on Series B, ever reached. Inside the window almost nobody gets to Series C, and I keep the figure low and nonzero for a breakout path with several quick rounds.

bands.rationale: Thin extension or flat round, used when growth slowed after the Series B and investors price the company on revenue multiples alone.
Central band; 2022 and later Series C median is $74M.
Strong growth round led by a large crossover or growth fund after the company shows durable revenue and net retention above 110 percent.
Category leader upside where the company is among the top two in its market and raises at a premium multiple to scale internationally.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C inside 10 months is almost out of reach: no voice company in the records reached it that fast. It would need an acquisition scale outcome in progress, such as a major lab bidding for the team, and rounds closing at breakneck pace, with each investor believing the model lead is durable against OpenAI, Google and Deepgram, which have far more compute.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Likely outcomes are a stall or acquihire as large voice labs and cloud providers ship low latency speech models, or a pivot to an application layer. Voicery (W18) shut down after big platforms offered speech synthesis, Uberduck (W22) is flagged inactive, and PlayAI sold to a large buyer, showing the range of exits for voice model teams.

killers.risk: Frontier labs and incumbents ship better low latency voice models
killers.evidence: OpenAI, Google and Deepgram offer real time voice APIs and keep reducing latency, so a two person lab can lose its edge within a release cycle.
killers.mitigation: Focus on one measurable latency and quality benchmark and sell to developers that need it.

killers.evidence: Training and serving interaction models costs real money while the team has only the YC deal and no stated customers.
killers.mitigation: Fine tune open models and sell usage early to fund compute.

killers.risk: Voice agent platforms capture the customer relationship
killers.evidence: Vapi and similar platforms choose models by price and latency, so the lab is a swappable supplier.
killers.mitigation: Offer an end to end agent product on its own models.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building speech models with low time to first audio and real conversation behaviour is research grade work needing compute and data. A two person team of researchers can reach a strong demo, but serving at scale, safety and keeping the lead are hard.

takeover_risk.rationale: Large labs and funded speech companies already release real time voice models and have distribution and compute, so any latency edge can narrow within a few quarters unless Talking Computers keeps shipping faster.

evidence.claim: Voice AI startups raised sharply more in recent years and voice agents are a paid use case
Several speech to speech startups raised early rounds on latency claims

narrative.headline: A hot voice model category but a two person lab with no stated traction; a priced seed inside 10 months is roughly one in three.
narrative.general_summary: Talking Computers is a two person AI lab building real time interaction models for voice agents. Voice is one of the most funded AI categories, and PlayAI and Vapi from earlier YC batches show that investors pay for voice models and infrastructure. The team has no stated customers and sits against Deepgram, Phonic, Smallest.ai and the large labs that all push latency down. For the 10 month window I take the AI cohort timing for seed and add only a small lift for the hot category. A Series A inside the window would need a breakout. The odds do not rank this company against others, and if it raises the most likely size is $3M to $6M or higher than usual for software.

assumptions: Only the input file was used about the company; no site or news was read.
Seed means a round above about $1M from outside investors, not the standard YC deal.
Search results dated after 2026-01-05 were ignored for the company and treated as market context only.
